correctness.rationale: After equilibrium substitution the source SDE is exactly dK=(A-delta K)dt+sigma sqrt(K)dW, i.e. a CIR square-root diffusion. The inspected primary distribution literature gives its noncentral-chi-square transition law and Gamma stationary law. The Gamma moments reproduce the source's own limiting mean and variance. The source explicitly defines D[K] as E[K^2]-E[K]^2, so its normal half-width 1.96 D uses variance instead of standard deviation. The benchmark controls, stationary shape/scale, quantiles, and coverages were independently recomputed by the bundled standard-library checker.

originality.rationale: The exact CIR distribution theory is classical, so novelty is restricted to its application to the 2022/2023 data-sharing game and the resulting correction of that paper's uncertainty bands. The source derives moments but assumes Normality and repeats the variance-width band in all three game regimes. Exact-title, DOI, CIR/Gamma, variance-band, and correction searches found no published source-specific correction. Indexed mathematical findings returned distributional and Gamma results in unrelated problems, not this stochastic game.
residual_risks: A non-indexed author note or later correction could contain the same source-specific observation.
The paper's simulation code was not available for inspection; a code-level band could in principle differ from the printed formulas.

value.rationale: The paper uses variance and its limiting value as a measure of risk and repeatedly attaches 95% bands to that risk analysis. For the published Nash benchmark the printed band is so wide that it extends below the nonnegative state space and has essentially 100% exact stationary coverage, whereas the exact Gamma 95% band is much narrower and asymmetric. Providing exact finite-time noncentral-chi-square and stationary Gamma bands directly repairs the model's uncertainty quantification without disturbing its equilibrium control analysis.
